notes:
Run 2026-10-20 23:07 UTC to 2026-10-21 01:40 UTC (date field is the task day; the run began on 2026-10-20 UTC) on a 4-vCPU / 15 GB shared VM, so absolute timings are noisy; ratios are the useful signal. grit = main at the commit above (release build, 0.5.15); git = system git 2.43.0; baseline = v0.5.0 release binary. GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM were isolated for all runs (the VM's global config enabled core.fsmonitor, which would have skewed git).
Harness: `grit-bench daily` run once per scenario (`--only`) instead of the single all-in-one run, because the all-in-one run aborts on the first scenario where the v0.5.0 baseline fails (v0.5.0 has no `blame` or `stash` command and `log` has no `--limit`). Those three headline rows therefore have baseline=null (not substituted). Each scenario ran with 1 warmup and 3 to 20 timed runs per tool (policy default; `runs` per tool is in each row). stddev_ms is null everywhere: the daily runner reports medians only. max_rss_kb is the peak RSS of the timed process tree (getrusage children maximum).
Measurement caveat found and corrected: grit-bench's capped-run helper polls children every 50 ms, which floors every timing under ~100 ms to a multiple of ~50 ms (first pass showed git and grit both at 50.6 ms for most fast commands). I did NOT change the repo. For the final numbers I copied the tree to /tmp, changed only the poll interval to 1 ms (and made the RSS sampler tolerate the /proc race at that rate) and re-measured every headline scenario and every scenario whose first-pass median was under 1 s, using the unmodified main-commit grit binary. Rows kept from the 50 ms-poll first pass (all >1 s, so quantisation is at most a few percent): clone/http@synth-10k, fetch/incremental-http@git-git, fsck/full@big-blobs, fsck/full@git-git, status/clean@deep-tree, status/dirty@deep-tree. The harness should get a lower poll interval or wait4-based timing.
Noise re-runs: bench-data did not exist, so there was no previous report to compare against; no regression-triggered re-runs were done (the quantisation re-measure above is the only re-run).
Failures / not measured: repack/full@git-git - grit gc repack on git.git ran over 14 minutes at 100% CPU with 7.7 GB peak RSS in a single run and was stopped (git side not recorded). push/incremental-http@git-git - produced no result within the 15 minute per-scenario cap. log/author@git-git is a pending placeholder in grit-bench (not measured, git and grit null). Baseline unavailable (v0.5.0 lacks the command): blame, log, stash.
Other observations: generating the many-refs-loose fixture with the in-process generator took about 9 minutes (roughly 12 loose refs/s). push/incremental@git-git was verified by hand: grit push updated the bare remote correctly and git fsck on it is clean, so the very low grit time is genuine. Large memory ratios: fsck/full@git-git grit uses about 26x git's peak RSS.
Headline scenario names/ids map 1:1 to the cooking page; the other scenarios use grit-bench's daily matrix (area values mapped: odb/packs/bundles->objects, index/diff->worktree, revwalk/blame/notes->history, remotes->remote, worktrees->branching, config/ignore/hooks->other).
